description: North Carolina Democrat seeks candidates for a communications fellowship. Competitive candidates will possess creativity, excellent writing skills, sound political judgement, and relevant prior experience. Expertise editing video or creating graphics a plus. Fellowship will require some remote and some in-person work, but can be fully remote to start. Diverse candidates and candidates with North Carolina ties are strongly encouraged to apply. Fellows will be paid a monthly stipend. To be considered, please submit a resume and 2-3 examples of your work (press release, social media post, op-ed draft, etc) to MacKensie Kvalvik at mackensie.kvalvik@mail.house.gov.
responsibilities: Perform communications-related work for a North Carolina Democratic office
Engage in both remote and in-person work
Edit video and create graphics as needed
qualifications: Expertise editing video or creating graphics (a plus)
how_to_apply: Submit a resume and 2-3 examples of your work (press release, social media post, op-ed draft, etc.) to MacKensie Kvalvik at mackensie.kvalvik@mail.house.gov.

description: Congresswoman Barragán's office is hiring a new cohort of interns to work this Summer in the San Pedro District office. Potential interns must be available to work in the San Pedro Office. Applications are being accepted on a rolling basis until positions are filled.
responsibilities: Attends committee meetings, intern conferences, and seminars.
Performs data entry, which involves logging in letters and constituent requests, including names and addresses of constituents.
Notes constituent opinions, including their full names, addresses, and all relevant information.
Greets visitors and signs for deliveries.
Performs other duties as assigned by the Intern Supervisor.
qualifications: Good oral and written communication skills.
Ability to work cooperatively and courteously with others.
Responsible, dependable, and willing to learn.

description: The Washington D.C. office of Congressman Matt Rosendale (MT-At Large) is currently seeking applicants for the full-time, paid intern position in the Summer of 2022. Interns are involved in all aspects of the office including constituent services (such as answering phones and constituent letters on a variety of issues), and legislative research, in addition to providing daily administrative and operational assistance. Interns are also encouraged to attend hearings, briefings, lectures, and seminars available in Congress and around the Hill. Ideal candidates are conservative college students or recent college graduates with strong communication and organizational skills. Students and recent graduates interested in learning more about our country's legislative process are encouraged to apply. Montana ties are preferred but by no means required. This internship will run for up to four months between May and August, with the specific start and end dates varying per individual applicant.
responsibilities: Providing constituent services such as answering phones and constituent letters on a variety of issues
Providing daily administrative and operational assistance
Attending hearings, briefings, lectures, and seminars available in Congress and around the Hill
qualifications: Conservative college student or recent college graduate
Interest in learning more about the country's legislative process
Montana ties preferred but not required
how_to_apply: E-mail resume and cover letter to alexandra.schindewolf@mail.house.gov with the subject line "Summer 2022 Internship." Please send all attachments as PDFs.

description: The Office of Congressman Kweisi Mfume (MD-07) is currently accepting applications for Summer 2022 in our Baltimore and DC offices. Interns will learn about the legislative process, constituent services, and many other functions of a congressional office. DC Intern responsibilities include: answering phones, researching legislation, attending virtual hearings and briefings, and answering constituent letters on various issues before the House. Interns will also assist in various administrative tasks as needed. Baltimore Intern responsibilities include: answering phones, assisting with casework, working on special projects in the district and other constituent related matters. The term of this internship will be from June – Early August. Paid full-time internships: must work at least 30 hours a week.
responsibilities: Learn about the legislative process, constituent services, and many other functions of a congressional office

DC Interns: answering constituent letters on various issues before the House

how_to_apply: Email a cover letter, resume, and short writing sample to Md07employment@mail.house.gov by noon on April 22, 2022. Note in the subject line 'Summer Internship' and which office you would prefer to work. No phone calls, follow-ups, or drop-ins.
equal_opportunity: All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, disability, or age.

description: Congressman Gregory W. Meeks (NY-5) is seeking an enthusiastic, highly motivated legislative and press/digital interns to work in-person in our Washington DC office for Summer 2022. Interns in Washington, D.C. are fully integrated into the day-to-day operations of our office. They are entrusted with a wide range of responsibilities to assist our legislative and communications staff. As an intern for Congressman Meeks, the Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and a senior member of the House Financial Services Committee, you will have a unique opportunity to gain unparalleled exposure to the political processes and legislative work on Capitol Hill.
qualifications: Willing to follow through on a wide variety of tasks
how_to_apply: Please submit your resume, cover letter, and 2-3-page writing sample and graphic sample (if applicable) to meeks.house.gov. Please submit your application no later than Friday, April 22nd at 11:59 PM EST.

description: Congressman Conor Lamb (PA-17) has openings for full and part-time congressional interns for his Washington, D.C. office during the Summer of 2022. Candidates should be motivated, flexible, and detail-oriented individuals with availability beginning in May, and a preference for those who can stay at least three months. Intern responsibilities include answering constituent phone calls, leading tours of the Capitol, sorting mail and faxes, and assisting staff with projects in diverse issue areas. Candidates should be outgoing and possess strong oral and written communication skills, an ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment, and a good sense of humor. Candidates with Pennsylvania ties and customer service experience are strongly encouraged to apply. There is a stipend and transit benefits available for qualifying candidates. Please e-mail a resume and cover letter including desired start date and availability to lamb.tours@mail.house.gov.

qualifications: Outgoing with strong oral and written communication skills
Ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment
Availability beginning in May with a preference for those who can stay at least three months
Pennsylvania ties and customer service experience strongly encouraged
how_to_apply: E-mail a resume and cover letter including desired start date and availability to lamb.tours@mail.house.gov.

description: Northwest Florida office is seeking summer interns in Washington, DC. The summer semester runs from May through August, dates are negotiable. The internship offers opportunities to gain hands-on experience working in a congressional office including legislative research, operations, and communications. Candidates enthusiastic about the America First movement are encouraged to apply. Interns' responsibilities will vary. The application deadline is on a rolling basis.
qualifications: Enthusiasm about the America First movement
how_to_apply: Send a resume and cover letter to northwestflorida000@gmail.com with the subject "Summer Internship Application". In your cover letter, please indicate expected start and end dates and hours available to work. The application deadline is on a rolling basis.

description: The Democratic staff of the House Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Government Operations, is seeking an energetic and self-motivated graduate or law school student for a full-time internship for Summer 2022. The position offers the opportunity to gain substantive experience on an exciting and fast-paced Subcommittee, while participating directly in the oversight process and learning about the day-to-day operations of the House of Representatives. The Committee on Oversight and Reform is the primary investigative committee of the U.S. House of Representatives, with jurisdiction to investigate any matter at any time. The Subcommittee on Government Operations has jurisdiction over issues related to the federal civil service, whistleblower protections, the U.S. Postal Service; government management and accounting measures; the economy, efficiency, and management of government operations and activities; government reorganization; intergovernmental affairs, including state and local governments; federal information technology security, acquisition policy, and management; and federal property.
responsibilities: Assisting staff in preparing for congressional hearings
Attending various briefings and meetings with Executive Branch and private sector officials
Working closely with Committee counsel and staff
qualifications: Ability to work well under pressure
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Willing to be in the office full time
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should apply by emailing their resume and cover letter in one PDF titled "last name, first name, Spring 2022 GovOps" to GovOpsSubcommittee@gmail.com with "Spring 2022 Internship Application" in the subject line. No phone calls or drop-ins please. Only applicants who are selected for an interview will receive a response.

description: Congresswoman María Elvira Salazar (FL-27) is currently accepting applicants for interns in her Miami and Washington, D.C. offices for the summer session. Core responsibilities include assisting in performing research, processing the mail, data entry, reception duties, and other office errands. Summer interns will begin their internship programs no earlier than May 1 and conclude their program no later than August 15. Interns are expected to serve in the office at a minimum of 15 hours each week during their tenure. The deadline for applications for the Summer 2022 internship session is April 30.
responsibilities: Attends community events and Congressional briefings
Performs data entry, which involves logging in letters and constituent requests, including names and addresses of constituents
Logs constituent correspondence, including their full names, addresses, and all other relevant information
Performs other duties as assigned by the intern coordinator of their office
qualifications: Good oral and written communication skills (Spanish language skills preferred)
Ability to work cooperatively and courteously with others
Ties to South Florida and means of travel are a plus
how_to_apply: Interested applicants may submit their resume and a cover letter to Howard Senior at hs@mail.house.gov (Miami) or Liam Diebel at liam.diebel@mail.house.gov (Washington, D.C.), in addition to completing the online application available at https://salazar.house.gov/services/internships.

description: The House Committee on Education and Labor (Democratic staff) seeks a fulltime Press Intern for paid and unpaid internships. Duties may include, but are not limited to, media monitoring and research, writing media advisories and press releases, drafting social media and general communications office support. Ideal candidate possesses strong writing skills, works well under pressure, and is a skilled multi-tasker. Interns can receive academic credit. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until June 1, 2022 for the summer and fall semesters. To apply, please email a cover letter, resume, three references, and two writing samples to E&L.Jobs@mail.house.gov with "Press Intern" in the subject line. Applications missing any of the requirements will not be considered. The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, or sexual orientation. Candidates of diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.
